label: copy-phase input n, late in long sequences
explanation: Fires only when the copy phase gets the token n as input, i.e. right after the model has output n. Copy-phase n input covers 99.97% of activations (dev), but on its own it has precision 0.17. Whether it fires and how strongly depends mainly on position. It never fires on an original-phase n or on the delimiter, and is almost silent before step 9. The firing rate climbs from about 0.1% at t=9 to about 2.6% at t=16-17, and long sequences (L=8-9) hold 90% of the activation mass. Gating to t >= 13 gives dev F1 0.64 with mass recall 0.91. Many late n inputs still do not fire, so the gate is incomplete. Top activations (about 4.0) appear when the original sequence ends in n n and the model is outputting the second n. When out_tok is also n, precision rises to 0.49, but this case is only about 16% of the mass. It fires on no tokens other than n (only 4 of 15077 dev activations).

scorecard.summary: Graded preference over the current input token (most: n, x, -, w, 1, z; least: o, g, 0, c) and the token being output (most: n, x, i, v, u, 1; least: t, 3, b, -); timing cues that raise it most: recall_idx=7, t=15, t=17.
